children: The Russian government has decided to extend restrictions on diesel exports for fuel producers until the end of October, Vedomosti daily reported late on Tuesday, citing two unidentified sources.
Russia introduced restrictions on exports of gasoline, jet fuel and diesel because of domestic fuel shortages exacerbated by Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries.
Vedomosti said the decision to extend the diesel export ban was taken following a meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak, President
point man on the oil sector.
Novak's office did not reply to a request for comment. The government has not officially announced whether it will extend the restrictions.
The current ban on diesel exports is due to expire at the end of September.

According to Reuters calculations based on data from fuel market participants, three of Russia's six largest diesel-producing refineries were forced to significantly cut output  or halt production altogether in September because of damage caused by drone attacks.
